subject: Physics
title: Laws of Motion
summary: Force CHANGES motion; it is not needed to keep motion going. With no net force a body stays in its state (rest or uniform velocity) — this is inertia (Newton's first law). Mass measures inertia.

Second law: net force = rate of change of momentum, F = dp/dt = ma (constant mass). A large force for a short time gives an impulse: J = FΔt = Δp. Third law: every action has an equal and opposite reaction — on different bodies, so they never cancel.

One method for every problem: isolate the body → draw its free-body diagram (FBD) → write ΣF = ma in each direction → add constraints (strings, contact). This solves pulleys, lifts, inclines and connected blocks.
Friction OPPOSES relative sliding. Static friction adjusts from 0 up to μ_s N as needed; once sliding starts, kinetic friction μ_k N acts (a little smaller). Rolling friction is the smallest.

Circular motion needs a net force towards the centre (centripetal, mv²/r) — not a new force; friction, tension, normal force or gravity provide it. On a level road it is friction; on a banked road a component of the normal force.

formulas.name: Newton's second law
formulas.formula: F_net = dp/dt = ma  (constant mass);   F_net = 0 ⇒ v constant
formulas.mistake: Write F_net, not just the applied force — include friction, weight, normal and every other force.

formulas.name: Momentum and impulse
formulas.formula: p = mv;   J = ∫F dt = F_avg Δt = Δp
formulas.when: Collisions, catching, bat and ball, bouncing.
formulas.mistake: For a bounce Δp = m(v + u) (direction reverses), not m(v − u).

formulas.name: Conservation of linear momentum
formulas.note: Apply it only in a direction where the external force is zero.

formulas.name: Recoil of gun
formulas.when: Backward kick of a gun on firing.
formulas.note: Opposite sign, smaller magnitude — the gun gets less kinetic energy.

formulas.name: Apparent weight in a lift
formulas.formula: Accelerating up: N = m(g + a);   accelerating down: N = m(g − a);   free fall: N = 0
formulas.mistake: Apparent weight changes with the lift's ACCELERATION, not its velocity.

formulas.name: Atwood machine
formulas.when: Two blocks hanging over one pulley (light string, smooth pulley).
formulas.mistake: T is never equal to m₁g (the heavier block accelerates downward).

formulas.name: Connected blocks (push/pull)
formulas.formula: a = F/(m₁ + m₂ + …);   contact force / tension = (total mass beyond the joint that this force pulls or pushes) × a
formulas.when: Blocks moving together on a smooth surface.
formulas.mistake: Find a contact force from the mass it pushes, not from the whole system.

formulas.name: Equilibrium of concurrent forces
formulas.formula: ΣF_x = 0, ΣF_y = 0;   Lami: F₁/sin α = F₂/sin β = F₃/sin γ
formulas.note: In Lami's theorem use the angle opposite each force (between the other two).

formulas.name: Static friction
formulas.formula: 0 ≤ f_s ≤ μ_s N;   limiting f = μ_s N
formulas.mistake: Static friction is not always μ_s N — it equals the applied force (up to the limit).

formulas.name: Kinetic friction
formulas.formula: f_k = μ_k N  (μ_k < μ_s), opposite to relative sliding
formulas.mistake: N is not always mg — on an incline it is mg cos θ; when pulled upward at an angle it is mg − F sin θ.

formulas.name: Angle of repose / friction
formulas.formula: tan θ_repose = μ_s;   angle of friction: tan λ = μ_s
formulas.when: Body just about to slide on an incline.
formulas.mistake: This comes from μ_s, not μ_k.

formulas.name: Block on rough incline
formulas.formula: Sliding down: a = g(sin θ − μ cos θ);   pushed up: a = −g(sin θ + μ cos θ)
formulas.note: Going up, friction also acts down the slope — the two add.

formulas.name: Centripetal force
formulas.mistake: Don't draw a separate 'centripetal force' in the FBD — it is the net inward force.

formulas.name: Vehicle on level road
formulas.note: Mass cancels — the same v_max for a truck and a bicycle.

formulas.name: Banked road
formulas.formula: Without friction: tan θ = v²/(rg).   With friction: v_max = √[rg(μ + tan θ)/(1 − μ tan θ)]
formulas.note: At the ideal speed no friction is needed; faster or slower, friction acts in different directions.

formulas.name: Pseudo force
formulas.formula: In a frame with acceleration a, apply −ma to every body
formulas.when: Problems seen from inside a lift or accelerating car.
formulas.mistake: Don't add a pseudo force when solving from the ground frame.

examples.title: Atwood machine
examples.problem: 5 kg and 3 kg hang from a light string over a smooth pulley (g = 10). Acceleration and tension?

examples.title: Friction: will it move?
examples.problem: 10 kg block, μ_s = 0.5, μ_k = 0.4 (g = 10). Apply (a) 40 N (b) 60 N — friction and acceleration?
examples.solution: Limiting friction = 0.5 × 100 = 50 N. (a) 40 < 50 ⇒ no motion, friction = 40 N (equal to the applied force). (b) 60 > 50 ⇒ slides; kinetic friction 40 N, a = (60 − 40)/10 = 2 m/s².

examples.title: Rough incline
examples.problem: A block slides down a 30° incline with μ_k = 0.2 (g = 10). Acceleration?

examples.title: Impulse from a bat
examples.problem: A 0.15 kg ball arrives at 20 m/s and goes back at 30 m/s after hitting the bat. Contact 0.01 s. Impulse and average force?

examples.title: Recoil of a gun
examples.problem: A 4 kg gun fires a 20 g bullet at 400 m/s. Recoil speed of the gun?
examples.solution: 0 = m_b v_b + M V ⇒ V = 0.02 × 400/4 = 2 m/s (opposite to the bullet).

examples.title: Angle of a banked road
examples.problem: A 100 m radius curve is designed for 20 m/s without friction (g = 10). Banking angle?

examples.title: Maximum speed on a level road
examples.problem: Flat curve of radius 50 m, μ_s = 0.4. Maximum speed without skidding?

examples.title: Weight in a lift
examples.problem: A 60 kg man stands in a lift accelerating at 2 m/s² (a) upward (b) downward. Machine reading (in N)?

examples.title: Weight hung by two strings
examples.problem: A 100 N weight hangs from two strings making 30° and 60° with the horizontal. Both tensions?
examples.solution: Horizontal: T₁ cos 30° = T₂ cos 60° ⇒ T₂ = √3 T₁. Vertical: T₁ sin 30° + T₂ sin 60° = 100 ⇒ T₁(0.5 + 1.5) = 100 ⇒ T₁ = 50 N, T₂ = 86.6 N. (The more vertical string carries more tension.)

examples.title: Pushing two blocks
examples.problem: 2 kg and 3 kg blocks touch on a smooth floor; the 2 kg block is pushed with 20 N. Contact force?
examples.solution: a = 20/5 = 4 m/s². Only the contact force pushes the 3 kg block ⇒ N = 3 × 4 = 12 N.

topics.title: Force and inertia
topics.explain: Force tries to change the state of motion. Inertia is the tendency not to change it; more mass = more inertia. When a bus starts suddenly we fall back (inertia of rest); when it stops we fall forward (inertia of motion).

topics.title: Newton's first law
topics.explain: With zero net force a body stays at rest or moves in a straight line at constant velocity. This law defines inertial frames. 'If it is moving, a force must be acting' is a wrong idea.

topics.title: Newton's second law and impulse
topics.explain: Momentum p = mv. F = dp/dt. Shorter time = larger force; that's why we pull our hands back while catching (increase time, reduce force) and why falling on a mattress hurts less.

topics.title: Newton's third law
topics.explain: An action–reaction pair is always equal, opposite, of the same type (both contact or both gravity) and acts on DIFFERENT bodies. For a book on a table, weight and normal force are not a pair (both act on the book).

topics.title: Applications of momentum conservation
topics.explain: Gun recoil, rockets (gas backward, rocket forward), explosions (zero total momentum before ⇒ zero after), a boat moving back when you jump off. Internal forces, however large, don't change total momentum.

topics.title: Laws of friction
topics.explain: (1) Friction is proportional to the normal reaction. (2) It is (nearly) independent of contact area. (3) μ_k < μ_s. (4) It depends on the nature of the surfaces. Friction opposes RELATIVE sliding, not motion — walking and driving forward rely on friction.

topics.title: Rolling friction
topics.explain: When a wheel rolls, the contact point is momentarily at rest, so there is no sliding friction; a small rolling friction arises from deformation. Hence ball bearings and wheels make work easier. Lubricants reduce both friction and wear.

topics.title: Circular motion: which force is centripetal?
topics.explain: Stone whirled on a string: tension. Car on a level road: static friction. Banked road: horizontal component of the normal force (+ friction). Satellite: gravity. In a vertical circle at the top: mg + T = mv²/r.

ratta: Lift: up a ⇒ m(g + a), down a ⇒ m(g − a), free fall ⇒ 0.
Atwood: a = (m₁ − m₂)g/(m₁ + m₂),  T = 2m₁m₂g/(m₁ + m₂).
f_s ≤ μ_s N;  f_k = μ_k N;  tan θ_repose = μ_s.
Incline down: a = g(sin θ − μ cos θ).
Level road v_max = √(μrg);  banking tan θ = v²/rg.
Action–reaction act on different bodies — never cancel.
